FAQ’s

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_accordion closed_toggle_text_color=”#2a2a2a” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#ffb400″ _builder_version=”4.16″ toggle_font=”Rubik|700|||||||” toggle_font_size=”18px” toggle_line_height=”1.4em” body_font=”||||||||” body_font_size=”15px” body_line_height=”1.8em” custom_margin=”||29px|||” custom_padding=”|||” border_width_all=”0px” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_accordion_item title=”I haven’t found my subject property, can I still apply? ” open=”on” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″]

Please feel free to go through the application leaving the subject property fields blank. However, you will not be able to lock-in an interest rate until a property has been selected.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”Does applying automatically lock in an interest rate? ” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ body_link_text_color=”#085c04″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″ open=”off”]

No. You should contact your Mortgage Loan Originator to lock-in your rate once a property has been identified.

 

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”I’m hesitant about divulging my personal information during the online application process. Is this site secure?” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ body_link_text_color=”#085c04″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″ open=”off”]

Our site uses secure internet protocols when transferring sensitive information. For a more complete explanation of our security policies, please see our Privacy Pledge. You may also contact a local Regions Mortgage Loan Originator directly to apply via phone or set-up an appointment to complete a loan application in person.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”Is there any financial obligation to completing the application? ” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ body_link_text_color=”#085c04″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″ open=”off”]

There are no fees associated with completing the Application information. Fees associated with originating a loan will not be collected until the application process is complete and you have received your initial RESPA documents.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”How long will it take to close this loan?” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ body_link_text_color=”#085c04″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″ open=”off”]

Generally we can close your loan comfortably within your interest rate lock period. However, if there are delays in submitting the required documentation, or there is a problem with your title work or appraisal, your lock period may not be sufficient.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”Can I choose my own appraiser?” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ body_link_text_color=”#085c04″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″ open=”off”]

Unfortunately, we cannot allow you to pick your own appraiser as this could present a potential conflict of interest situation. Regions requires that appraisals be performed by pre-approved appraisers who are selected at random based on property location via a third party vendor.

[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”What type documentation is typically requested with my loan application? ” open_toggle_text_color=”#4a1009″ open_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” closed_toggle_background_color=”#ffffff” icon_color=”#4a1009″ _builder_version=”4.16″ body_link_text_color=”#085c04″ custom_margin=”1px||1px||true” global_colors_info=”{}” toggle_text_color=”#085c04″ open=”off”]

Following are some of the documents you will be requested to provide to your Mortgage Loan Originator at the time of application:

  • A two-year history of residence
  • Names, addresses and telephone numbers of landlords for the past two years
  • Employer’s name and address for the last two years
  • Salaried Applicants:  Most recent two years’ W-2 forms and two most recent paystubs.
  • Commissioned Applicants:  Most recent two years’ 1040 tax forms (including supporting schedules) and YTD income statement.
  • Self-Employed Applicants:  Most recent two years’ signed personal/corporate tax returns (with supporting schedules) and current Profit and Loss Statement and Balance Sheet.
  • Two most recent bank statements (checking, savings, etc.)

Linda Lemoine

Linda Lemoine-Ueckert has been in the real estate/mortgage lending business for over 30 years.  Linda is passionate about what she does and takes great pride in her work ethics and customer service.  She listens to the needs and wants of her clients making sure to guide them through the mortgage lending process by holding their hands and collaborating with clients to help pursue their goal of homeownership.  

Linda spent over 25 years as Vice President of the Mortgage Department working for several local banks before becoming a partner with Magnolia State Mortgage. LLC.  Linda is a graduate of Louisiana College, a member of NAMB, La Mortgage Lenders Association and has participated in many civic organizations in leadership roles and believes in practicing philanthropy to better our community. When not working she enjoys spending time with family and friends boating, enjoying sunsets and working in the flower garden.

Marci LaBorde

Marci has been a mortgage loan originator since 2002.  She is one of the founding partners at Magnolia State Mortgage, which opened in April 2006.  Her 35-year background also includes Small Business Management, Real Estate, Home Building Project Manager/Designer.  With this background and her work experience, she knows communication is the key to creating a great relationship with clients.  She loves working with first-time buyers, those moving up and those building a home.

Marci received a B.S. from Texas State University in Business Management and Education.    She is a Member of NAMB, LA Mortgage Lending Associate, Central Louisiana Chamber of Commerce, Affiliate with Greater Central Louisiana Realtors Association and active member of her Church.
